questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the electron is a fundamental lepton.
questions.feedbackWrong: Protons and neutrons are baryons (made of quarks); pions are mesons. The electron is a fundamental lepton.

mistakes.misconception: Confuses mesons with leptons because both are light.
mistakes.correction: Pions are mesons — quark-antiquark pairs, not fundamental. Leptons are fundamental particles with no quark structure.

questions.prompt: Describe what happens when an electron meets its antiparticle, the positron, and state what the products are.

markScheme.text: The electron and positron annihilate — both particles are destroyed.
Their total mass-energy is converted into electromagnetic radiation per $E = mc^2$.
Two photons (gamma rays) are produced travelling in opposite directions, conserving momentum.

mistakes.misconception: Produces a single photon from annihilation.
mistakes.correction: A single photon cannot conserve momentum — annihilation at rest produces two photons in opposite directions.

questions.prompt: A stone is dropped from rest from a height of 45 m. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², calculate the time taken to reach the ground in seconds.
According to Newton's third law, the reaction force to a book's weight pressing on a table is:
options: The table pushing up on the book
The book pulling gravitationally on the Earth
The Earth pulling down on the table
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — the Newton III pair to the Earth's pull on the book is the book's pull on the Earth.
questions.feedbackWrong: Newton III pairs act on DIFFERENT bodies and are the same type of force: the weight is Earth's gravitational pull on the book, so its pair is the book's gravitational pull on Earth.

mistakes.misconception: Pairs weight with the normal contact force — the classic misconception.
mistakes.correction: Weight and normal force act on the SAME body and are different types of force — they cannot be a Newton III pair, even when equal in size.

questions.prompt: A 1200 kg car travelling at 15 m/s collides with and sticks to a stationary 800 kg car. Calculate their common velocity immediately after the collision in m/s.
Explain why the horizontal and vertical motions of a projectile can be treated independently, and state what this implies about the horizontal velocity during flight (neglecting air resistance).

markScheme.text: The only force acting is gravity, which is entirely vertical — no horizontal force exists.
Perpendicular components of motion do not affect each other — acceleration in one direction leaves the perpendicular component unchanged.
Therefore horizontal velocity remains CONSTANT throughout the flight.
While vertical velocity changes by g each second — the two combine to give the parabolic path.

mistakes.misconception: Believes horizontal speed decays even without air resistance.
mistakes.correction: With no horizontal force there is no horizontal acceleration — the horizontal component is constant by Newton's first law.

questions.prompt: What is the quark composition of a proton?
questions.feedbackCorrect: Correct — proton is two up quarks and one down quark.
questions.feedbackWrong: Proton = uud (charge +2/3 +2/3 −1/3 = +1); the neutron is udd.

mistakes.correction: udd gives charge 0 — that's the neutron. The proton needs two up quarks for its +1 charge.

questions.prompt: A crane lifts a 500 kg load through 12 m at constant speed. Taking g = 9.81 m/s², calculate the work done by the crane and explain why it equals the gain in gravitational potential energy.

markScheme.text: Constant speed means zero net force, so the lifting force equals the weight: $F = mg = 500 \times 9.81$.
At constant speed no kinetic energy is gained, so by conservation of energy all the work done transfers to gravitational potential energy.
